review_notes: I read the whole file. The group, IntermediateField and Laurent lemmas are standalone theorems, which the rubric excludes. I grepped the project's Definitions for competing definitions and found one concrete duplication: `qExpAlg` has the same body as three existing project definitions. Mathlib has no `qExpand`-based AlgHom of its own. I did not check whether the target transitively imports `X0ModL` or `CharLFrobeniusGeomLevel`. `Def_ModularCurve_X0` is reachable through `JqCoeff`, so `qExpandₐ` is available for ℚ. `charZero_of_algebraRat` is a theorem and is excluded. I found no competing Mathlib definition for `anSet`, `AA`, `FF`, `GA` or `GB`.

findings.excerpt:
def qExpAlg (ℓ : ℕ) [NeZero ℓ] : LaurentSeries K →ₐ[K] LaurentSeries K where
  __ := qExpand K ℓ
findings.problem: `qExpAlg` is the AlgHom packaging of `qExpand K ℓ` on `LaurentSeries K`. The project already defines the same object under other names with the same body and the same `_apply` lemma. These are `ModularCurve.qExpandAlgC` in Def_ModularCurve_CharLFrobeniusGeomLevel, `ModularCurve.qExpandAlgHomC` in Def_ModularCurve_X0ModL, and `qExpandₐ` (ℚ only) in Def_ModularCurve_X0. This file adds a fourth copy, with a redundant `coe_qExpAlg`. Results about `.map (qExpAlg K ℓ)` do not transfer to `.map (qExpandAlgC K ℓ)`, because the two are different constants. Users need `show` or `rfl` conversions to move between them. The file already uses `qExpAlg ℚ ℓ` where `qExpandₐ ℓ` would do.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `qExpAlg`, `qExpAlg_apply` and `coe_qExpAlg`. Reuse one existing definition and move it to an upstream file that all three can import. Either use `ModularCurve.qExpandAlgHomC` / `qExpandAlgC`, or make `qExpandₐ` its ℚ instance. If the name `qExpAlg` is wanted, add `local notation` or an `abbrev` for the shared definition. The lemmas `adjoin_qExpand_image`, `laurentBaseChange_map` and `map_FF_Gamma1_le` then apply unchanged.
findings.benefit: There would be one AlgHom wrapper of `qExpand`, so `IntermediateField.map` statements and `commutes'` proofs are not duplicated. The `X1LDMain` and `X1GEN2` results would then also compose with the existing Frobenius and degeneracy API without conversions.
